title: Umayyad Caliphate
summary: Muawiya, governor of Syria, founded the Umayyad dynasty in 661, the first dynasty to hold the caliphate, and ruled from Damascus. Under the Umayyads the caliphate reached its greatest extent, adding North Africa beyond Egypt, most of Spain by 714, Transoxiana and parts of the Indian subcontinent. The Umayyad Great Mosque of Damascus remains one of the oldest sites of continuous Muslim prayer. Civil wars weakened the dynasty, and the Abbasids overthrew it in 750.

uncertainty.note: Established in 661 CE following the accession of Muawiya I; overthrown by the Abbasid Revolution in 750 CE.

as_recorded.value: The Umayyad Dynasty (661-750 CE), the first dynasty to take the title of Caliphate, was established in 661 CE by Muawiya
In particular, the Umayyad caliphate created Damascus as its capital

where.historical_name: Damascus, capital of the Umayyad Caliphate

importance.justification: Carried Muslim rule from Spain to Transoxiana and set the first dynastic caliphate (R3 D4 T3 L3).

related.because: The overthrow of the Umayyad Caliphate in the 750 CE Abbasid Revolution led directly to the establishment of the Abbasid Caliphate.
